| Options | Generated section-aware `Configure<TSettings>` registration on opt-in models |
| Validation | `IValidateOptions<TSettings>` backed by a generated Valiant validator |
| UI | Built-in schema explorer and JSON endpoint with safe secret masking |
| Tooling | `IValiantSettingsSchemaProvider` for custom consumers |

#### Documentation map

- [Quick start](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/quick-start/)
- [Runnable samples](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/samples/)
- [Schema generation](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/guides/schema-generation/)
- [Binding and validation](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/guides/binding-validation/)
- [ASP.NET Core UI](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/guides/aspnetcore-ui/)
- [Schema API, generation, and diagnostics](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/reference/schema-api/)

The [sample catalog](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/samples/) covers every selectable core and ASP.NET
Core scenario for schema metadata, binding, validation, and the safe-by-default
UI.
### Quick start

#### 1. Choose a package

```bash
# Schema generation and optional Options binding
dotnet add package StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings

# Or install a specific integration
dotnet add package StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore
dotnet add package StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Validation
```

Specific integration packages forward the core runtime, build, and generator assets they depend on. Add multiple integration packages only when the application uses multiple integrations.

#### 2. Mark a settings model

```csharp
using StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings;

[ValiantSettings("Mail", configure: true)]
public sealed record MailSettings
{
    public required string Host { get; init; }
    public int Port { get; init; } = 587;

    [ValiantSecret]
    public string? Password { get; init; }
}
```

The section path is required. `configure: true` opts this model into generated Options binding; omit it for schema-only metadata.

#### 3. Register generated settings

```csharp
using StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.DependencyInjection;

builder.Services.AddValiantSettings(builder.Configuration);
```

The generated extension binds opted-in models and registers every generated schema provider.

#### 4. Consume the options

```csharp
public sealed class MailSender(IOptions<MailSettings> options)
{
    private readonly MailSettings _settings = options.Value;
}
```

Or enumerate schemas:

```csharp
IEnumerable<IValiantSettingsSchemaProvider> schemas =
    provider.GetServices<IValiantSettingsSchemaProvider>();
```

Next: learn how nested models and collections appear in [Schema generation](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/guides/schema-generation/).
### Settings samples

Settings has separate console and ASP.NET Core sample projects. In each project,
select one delegate or startup near the top of `Program.cs`.

Settings source generation is assembly-wide. Selecting one scenario changes
which code runs, but every `[ValiantSettings]` model in that project contributes
to `ValiantSettingsSchemas` and the generated `AddValiantSettings` method. The
samples therefore use distinct section paths.

#### Core settings

Run the console project:

```bash
dotnet run --project settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Samples
```

Select one delegate in
[`Program.cs`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/blob/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Samples/Program.cs):

| Delegate | Demonstrates | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Basic.Sample.Run` | The normal configured-settings flow: `[ValiantSettings(..., configure: true)]`, `AddValiantSettings(configuration)`, and `IOptions<TSettings>` consumption | [`Basic`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Samples/Basic) |
| `RegistrationOptions.Sample.Run` | Default schema-provider registration compared with `RegisterSchemaProviders = false`, while configured Options still bind | [`RegistrationOptions`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Samples/RegistrationOptions) |
| `SchemaRegistry.Sample.Run` | `ValiantSettingsSchemas.All`, `Get<TSettings>`, and successful and unsuccessful `TryGet<TSettings>` lookups | [`SchemaRegistry`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Samples/SchemaRegistry) |
| `SchemaMetadata.Sample.Run` | Property kinds, nested objects, collections, nullability, required members, and secret metadata | [`SchemaMetadata`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Samples/SchemaMetadata) |

`SchemaMetadata` also shows that a runtime property initializer is not emitted
as schema `DefaultValue` metadata.

#### ASP.NET Core settings

Run the web project:

```bash
dotnet run --project settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples
```

Select one startup type in
[`Program.cs`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/blob/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/Program.cs):

| Startup | Demonstrates | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Basic.Startup` | `AddValiantSettings()` and the default `/_valiant/settings` explorer and schema routes | [`Basic`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/Basic) |
| `Configuration.Startup` | A custom `/admin/settings` path and authorization conventions on the returned `RouteGroupBuilder` | [`Configuration`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/Configuration) |
| `RuntimeValues.Startup` | `ShowRuntimeValues = true`, explicit secret masking, defensive name-based masking, and reveal disabled | [`RuntimeValues`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/RuntimeValues) |
| `SecretReveal.Startup` | `AllowSecretReveal = true` with explicit `?revealSecrets=true` opt-in | [`SecretReveal`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/SecretReveal) |
| `Validation.Startup` | `ValidateWithValiant = true` with permissive behavior when a configured model has no validator | [`Validation`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/Validation) |
| `Validation.InvalidStartup` | Valiant failures translated into `OptionsValidationException` failures | [`Validation`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/Validation) |
| `Validation.RequiredStartup` | `RequireValidators = true` failing when a configured settings model has no matching validator | [`Validation`](https://github.com/static-north-dev/valiant/tree/main/settings/samples/StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore.Samples/Validation) |

The three validation startups intentionally share one folder because they use
the same settings models and validators while exercising different registration
policies.

#### Try the web scenarios

With the HTTP launch profile running on port `5194`:

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:5194/_valiant/settings
curl -i -H "X-Settings-Admin: true" http://localhost:5194/admin/settings
curl -s http://localhost:5194/runtime-values/schemas
curl -s "http://localhost:5194/secret-reveal/schemas?revealSecrets=true"
curl -i http://localhost:5194/validation/invalid
```

The configuration sample uses a deliberately small header-based demo
authentication handler. Replace it with the host application's real
authentication and authorization policy.

Runtime values and secret reveal are administrative capabilities. Protect the
returned route group before enabling either outside local development. See
[ASP.NET Core UI](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/guides/aspnetcore-ui/) and
[Binding and validation](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/guides/binding-validation/) for the production
configuration.
### Schema generation

`[ValiantSettings]` is the generator discovery boundary. It produces a deterministic `ValiantSettingsSchema` for the marked type.

```csharp
[ValiantSettings("Search")]
public sealed record SearchSettings
{
    public required Uri Endpoint { get; init; }
    public SearchRetrySettings Retry { get; init; } = new();
    public string[] Indexes { get; init; } = [];
}

public sealed record SearchRetrySettings
{
    public int Attempts { get; init; } = 3;
    public TimeSpan Delay { get; init; } = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1);
}
```

The model schema contains its CLR type, display name, section path, and ordered property schemas. Each property records:

- CLR name and configuration key;
- type display name and normalized kind;
- C# required-member and nullability flags;
- secret flag and declared compile-time constant initializer, when available for a non-sensitive property;
- nested object properties or collection item schema.

Public instance properties with public getters are included, including inherited properties. The most derived declaration wins when a property is overridden or hidden. Overrides retain an inherited `[ValiantSecret]` marker.

#### Property kinds

| Kind | Represents |
| --- | --- |
| `String` | Text and string-like configuration values |
| `Boolean` | Boolean values |
| `Integer` | Integral numeric values |
| `Number` | Floating-point and decimal values |
| `Enum` | Enum values |
| `Object` | Nested settings object |
| `Array` | Array or collection with an item schema |
| `Unknown` | A type without a more specific schema classification |

#### Schema-only or configured

Schema generation always occurs. Binding is opt-in:

```csharp
[ValiantSettings("Features")]
public sealed record FeatureCatalog; // schema only

[ValiantSettings("Features", configure: true)]
public sealed record BoundFeatureCatalog; // schema + Options binding
```

This lets libraries publish metadata without changing the host's service graph.

#### Secret metadata

```csharp
[ValiantSecret]
public string? ClientSecret { get; init; }
```

`ValiantSecret` tells schema consumers that runtime values must be hidden. The ASP.NET Core UI also masks common sensitive names defensively, but explicit attributes are the durable contract for custom tools.

:::info Deterministic output
Generated schemas are stable enough for tooling to sort, diff, cache, and render. No runtime type scan is required to discover marked settings models.
:::
### Binding and validation

#### Generated Options binding

Set `configure: true` and register settings once:

```csharp
[ValiantSettings("Storage:S3", configure: true)]
public sealed record S3Settings
{
    public required string Bucket { get; init; }
    public string? Region { get; init; }
}

builder.Services.AddValiantSettings(builder.Configuration);
```

Valiant emits the equivalent section-aware `services.Configure<S3Settings>(configuration.GetSection("Storage:S3"))` registration.

Use `[ConfigurationKeyName("bucket-name")]` from `Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration` to give a property a different configuration key. The generated schema and runtime values use that key, and the schema retains the CLR property name. On .NET 11, properties marked `[ConfigurationIgnore]` are excluded from binding and from the generated schema and runtime values.

Schema providers register by default. Disable them when the application only needs binding and validation:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddValiantSettings(builder.Configuration, options =>
{
    options.RegisterSchemaProviders = false;
});
```

#### Validate Options with Valiant

Reference `StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Validation` and declare the matching validator:

```csharp
[ValiantValidator]
public sealed partial class S3SettingsValidator
    : ValidatorDefinition<S3Settings>
{
    public override void Configure(ValidationContext<S3Settings> context)
    {
        context.Property(settings => settings.Bucket).Required();
        context.Property(settings => settings.Region).MaxLength(32);
    }
}
```

Register validators and enable the adapter:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddValiantValidators();
builder.Services.AddValiantSettings(builder.Configuration, options =>
{
    options.ValidateWithValiant = true;
});
```

Generated settings registration adds `IValidateOptions<S3Settings>` for configured settings models. It resolves a matching `IValidator<S3Settings>` from DI and translates Valiant errors to normal Options validation failures.

#### Await validation at startup on .NET 11

Alongside the Valiant registration above, opt each settings model into startup validation:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddOptions<S3Settings>().ValidateOnStart();
```

The .NET 11 adapter implements `IAsyncValidateOptions<S3Settings>`. The host awaits the Valiant validator's `ValidateAsync` method during startup, passes the startup cancellation token, and reports validation errors in an `OptionsValidationException`.

Read async-only settings from `IOptions<S3Settings>.Value` after startup completes. Configuration reloads and new `IOptionsSnapshot<S3Settings>` scopes create options synchronously and require validators that support synchronous validation.

#### Require matching validators

By default, validation succeeds when no validator is registered. Make missing validators a configuration error:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddValiantSettings(builder.Configuration, options =>
{
    options.ValidateWithValiant = true;
    options.RequireValidators = true;
});
```

Only models with `configure: true` receive Options binding and validation adapters. Schema-only models remain metadata contracts.
### ASP.NET Core UI

`StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore` provides a compact settings explorer and a JSON document backed by generated schema providers.

```csharp
using StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore;
using StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.DependencyInjection;

builder.Services.AddValiantSettings(builder.Configuration);

var app = builder.Build();
app.MapValiantSettingsUi();
```

The default routes are:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/_valiant/settings` | Interactive schema explorer |
| `/_valiant/settings/schemas` | Generated schema JSON document |

#### Change the route

```csharp
app.MapValiantSettingsUi(options =>
    options.Path = "/admin/settings");
```

The JSON endpoint follows the prefix at `/admin/settings/schemas`.

#### Show current runtime values

```csharp
app.MapValiantSettingsUi(options =>
{
    options.ShowRuntimeValues = true;
});
```

Runtime values come from the host's default `IOptions<TSettings>` instance for each registered schema. The explorer reports values as unavailable when the host has neither Options configuration for that model nor an explicitly supplied options instance. Runtime values can include defaults and values assigned by configuration or post-configuration. Declared defaults in the property list describe constant initializers.

The explorer loads the schema catalog first and requests values for the selected section when you open its Runtime view. Changing sections clears revealed values. A request to `/schemas` without a section selector still returns the full document.

#### Protect secrets

`[ValiantSecret]` properties are masked. Valiant also masks common sensitive names such as `Password`, `Secret`, `Token`, `ApiKey`, `ClientSecret`, and `ConnectionString`.

Explicitly permit reveal only when endpoint authorization and hosting policy make it acceptable:

```csharp
RouteGroupBuilder settings = app.MapValiantSettingsUi(options =>
{
    options.ShowRuntimeValues = true;
    options.AllowSecretReveal = true;
});

settings.RequireAuthorization("SettingsAdministrators");
```

Secret values remain masked until a user selects reveal. The JSON endpoint accepts `?revealSecrets=true` only when `AllowSecretReveal` is enabled.

Masked secret getters are not evaluated. Runtime values are projected through the generated schema: recursive objects beyond the schema boundary become empty objects, and unsupported opaque values become `null`. Options or getter failures return a generic message so exception text cannot expose credentials. Schema responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`, including when secrets are revealed.

Direct callers of `ValiantSettingsSchemaDocumentFactory.Create` must also enable both `revealSecrets` and `canRevealSecrets` to reveal values.

:::danger Treat the explorer as an administrative endpoint
The package does not decide your authorization policy. Protect the returned `RouteGroupBuilder`, especially when runtime values or secret reveal are enabled.
:::

Run the default UI, custom authorization, runtime-value masking, and explicit
secret-reveal variants from the [Settings sample catalog](https://valiant.staticnorth.dev/settings/samples/#aspnet-core-settings).
### Schema API, generation, and diagnostics

#### Provider contract

Each generated provider implements:

```csharp
public interface IValiantSettingsSchemaProvider
{
    Type SettingsType { get; }
    string? SectionPath { get; }
    ValiantSettingsSchema Schema { get; }
}
```

Resolve all providers to build custom documentation, editors, configuration audits, or deployment tooling:

```csharp
foreach (var provider in services.GetServices<IValiantSettingsSchemaProvider>())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{provider.Schema.Name}: {provider.SectionPath}");

    foreach (var property in provider.Schema.Properties)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"  {property.ConfigurationKey} ({property.Kind})");
    }
}
```

#### Model schema

`ValiantSettingsSchema` exposes `SettingsType`, `Name`, `SectionPath`, and `Properties`.

`ValiantSettingsPropertySchema` exposes:

- `Name`, `ConfigurationKey`, and `TypeName`;
- `Kind`, `IsRequired`, `IsNullable`, and `IsSecret`;
- `DefaultValue` when it is known at generation time;
- `Item` for arrays/collections;
- `Properties` for nested objects.

#### ASP.NET Core document

The UI JSON endpoint returns `ValiantSettingsSchemaDocument`. It contains ordered `ValiantSettingsSchemaEntry` values and indicates whether secrets can be revealed and whether the current response contains revealed values. Each entry can include masked runtime values or a runtime-value resolution error.

#### Packages

| Package | Use it for | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings` | Schema generation and optional Options binding | .NET 8 and .NET Standard 2.0 |
| `StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.AspNetCore` | Built-in explorer and JSON schema endpoint | .NET 8 |
| `StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Validation` | Options validation through Valiant validators | .NET 8 |

Integration packages forward their parent runtime and generator assets. `StaticNorth.Valiant.Settings.Validation` also carries the core Valiant Validation assets it integrates with.

#### Generator scope and diagnostics

Only types marked with `[ValiantSettings]` enter the incremental generator pipeline. Generated output includes the schema provider and, when the required Microsoft configuration/DI APIs are referenced, the aggregated `AddValiantSettings` registration surface.

| ID | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `VLS001` | Generic settings model types are not supported |
| `VLS002` | The settings section path is empty |

The section path is deliberately required so generated binding and external tooling share one unambiguous configuration identity.
